# clankers-kit

An opt-in setup for Claude Code and Codex, in one repo you own. It composes `~/.claude`,
`~/.agents` and `~/.codex` from one instructions file, a catalog of skills, hooks that block,
and per-project memory. Clone it, run `./setup.sh`, then make it yours.

> The name comes from
> [clanker](https://lucumr.pocoo.org/2026/5/26/clankers/), a mechanical word for the machine you
> engineer.

<!-- The demo GIF is generated by demo/demo.tape (see CONTRIBUTING.md). -->

![setup.sh running](assets/setup-demo.gif)

## The idea

A coding agent does not work the way you work. So configure it:

- an `AGENTS.md` the agent reads every turn, with your role and your conventions;
- a skill for each multi-step task you repeat, called by name;
- a hook for each rule that must hold, because a hook blocks the write instead of asking;
- per-project memory the agent writes and re-reads, so context builds up.

Then extend it. Each time you correct the agent twice, write the next line of `AGENTS.md`, the
next hook, or the next skill. This is a starter you own, not a dependency you install.

## Quick start

You need `bash`, `git` and [`jq`](https://jqlang.github.io/jq/) on macOS or Linux.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/e-krebs/clankers-kit.git ~/Projects/clankers-kit
cd ~/Projects/clankers-kit && ./setup.sh
```

`setup.sh` detects your agents, then shows one picker where every row is on by default except
the skill trigger hooks. It ends with a recap and waits for one confirmation. It adopts an
existing `AGENTS.md` or `settings.json` and never overwrites it, and a re-run leaves a linked
path alone. `./setup.sh --sandbox` does the whole run against a throwaway `HOME`.

Then open `.agents/AGENTS.md` and write how you work, and restart Claude Code.
[docs/setup.md](docs/setup.md) covers the picker, the flags, the layout and the uninstall.

> [!WARNING]
> Codex runs a hook only once you trust its definition. Open `codex` and run `/hooks` after
> setup, and again after any re-run that changes the wiring.

## What's inside

| Piece                        | What it is                                                                                                             |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `kit.json`                   | The manifest: every row `setup.sh` offers, its group, its defaults, its requirements.                                  |
| `.agents/AGENTS.example.md`  | A worked example of a personal instructions file.                                                                      |
| `.agents/AGENTS.template.md` | A blank version `setup.sh` fills in for you.                                                                           |
| `.agents/skills/`            | The [skill catalog](.agents/skills/README.md): a workflow family, a review family, TypeScript tips.                    |
| `.agents/hooks/`             | The shared hook scripts, their `hooks.json` fragments, the composer, the fixtures. See [docs/hooks.md](docs/hooks.md). |
| `.agents/workflow-profiles/` | Per-org and per-repo tables the workflow skills read: ticket system, commit policy, CI watcher, verify commands.       |
| `.claude/settings/`          | Opt-in setting presets, merged additively: the safe-command allowlist, the Plain-by-default style, `base.json`.        |
| `.claude/output-styles/`     | The Plain output style: Simplified Technical English, five units per reply, no bold.                                   |
| `.claude/projects/`          | Where the per-project memory is tracked.                                                                               |

Any agent that reads `~/.agents` picks up the skills and the workflow profiles. The kit links
the instructions file and the hook wiring per agent, and it wires Claude Code and Codex today.
A port to another agent adds a link row to `kit.json`, see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).

> [!WARNING]
> Your memories are tracked, so keep your fork private. `.claude/projects/*/memory` can hold
> private, work-specific detail. Scrub that directory before you push anywhere public.
> `setup.sh` offers to flip your repo private for this reason.

## Build your own

Read `.agents/AGENTS.example.md`, then rewrite it as you. Add a hook when you catch the agent
doing something you keep correcting, and a skill when you repeat the same multi-step task. Both
need a row in `kit.json`, a `bash .agents/lint-manifest.sh` run, and a `./setup.sh` re-run.
[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) has the details.
